cards.lore: Externalized PS is a macrophage eat me signal. Statins reduce cholesterol synthesis, altering membrane lipid composition and signaling.
cards.power: Flippase Swap — Burn ATP to move Phosphatidylserine (PS) to the inner leaflet.

cards.lore: Digitalis inhibits Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase → intracellular Na⁺ rises → Ca²⁺ extrusion via NCX drops → cardiac contractility increases.
cards.power: Primary Active Transport — Maintain the resting potential gradient to drive secondary co-transport.

cards.lore: Cholera toxin ADP-ribosylates Gsα, locking it in the GTP-bound active state → massive cAMP → CFTR activation → fatal secretory diarrhoea.
cards.power: Second Messenger Swarm — Exchange GDP for GTP on Gα to activate adenylyl cyclase or PLC-β.

cards.lore: Constitutive activation of the RAS/MAPK cascade via KRAS mutations renders colorectal tumors completely resistant to anti-EGFR therapies like cetuximab.
cards.power: Dimerize & Destroy — Bind extracellular growth factor to trans-autophosphorylate intracellular tyrosine residues.

cards.lore: Corticosteroids block this by upregulating IκBα transcription and directly transrepressing p65. Bortezomib kills myeloma cells by blocking IκB proteasomal degradation.
cards.power: IκB Degradation — Trigger the proteasome to destroy the IκB inhibitor, freeing NF-κB to enter the nucleus.

cards.lore: Amino acids (especially leucine) recruit mTORC1 to the lysosomal surface. Rapamycin targets this complex to induce profound immunosuppression.
cards.power: Anabolic Trigger — If amino acids and ATP are high, phosphorylate S6K1 to drive ribosome biogenesis.

cards.lore: APC is the gatekeeper of colorectal cancer. Truncated APC fails to degrade β-catenin, driving the relentless adenoma-carcinoma sequence.
cards.power: β-catenin Accumulation — Inhibit the GSK-3β destruction complex to allow β-catenin to transcribe c-Myc and cyclin D1.

cards.lore: PTCH1 loss-of-function drives Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC). Vismodegib shrinks these tumors dramatically by directly inhibiting the downstream SMO.
cards.power: Smoothened Derepression — Bind Hedgehog ligand to internalize PTCH1 and free SMO to activate GLI transcription factors.

cards.lore: NOTCH1 activating mutations drive >60% of T-ALL. γ-secretase inhibitors failed as Alzheimer's drugs due to extreme GI toxicity from goblet cell metaplasia.
cards.power: Lateral Inhibition — Upon adjacent ligand binding, release NICD to repress alternative cell fate genes.

cards.lore: VHL mutation stabilizes HIF-1α regardless of oxygen, creating a highly vascular pseudo-hypoxic state in clear cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
cards.power: VEGF Summon — Evade VHL-mediated ubiquitination to transcribe angiogenesis and glycolysis genes.

cards.lore: PFK-1 is the rate-limiting step. ¹⁸F-FDG PET imaging exploits the Warburg effect by trapping phosphorylated glucose analogue (FDG-6-P) inside voracious tumors.
cards.power: Warburg Shift — Override mitochondrial limits to preferentially run aerobic glycolysis for rapid ATP and biosynthesis.

cards.lore: Thiamine (B1) deficiency halts α-KG dehydrogenase. Giving IV glucose without thiamine to an alcoholic precipitates fatal Wernicke's encephalopathy.
cards.power: NADH Generation — Oxidize Acetyl-CoA to CO₂ to capture high-energy electrons.

cards.lore: Cyanide halts Complex IV (cytochrome oxidase) by binding Fe³⁺. Treat with hydroxocobalamin and amyl nitrite to induce methaemoglobin as a cyanide decoy.
cards.power: Proton Gradient — Pump H⁺ to the intermembrane space to create the electrochemical gradient for ATP synthase.

cards.lore: PDH deficiency causes severe lactic acidosis. A ketogenic diet bypasses PDH by supplying brain energy via β-hydroxybutyrate.
cards.power: Irreversible Commitment — Convert pyruvate to Acetyl-CoA. Once crossed, carbons cannot return to glucose.

cards.lore: MCAD deficiency prevents medium-chain fat oxidation. Fasting triggers lethal hypoketotic hypoglycaemia because alternative fuels cannot be synthesized.
cards.power: Carnitine Shuttle — Exchange acylcarnitine for free carnitine to breach the inner mitochondrial membrane.

cards.lore: The liver produces ketones but lacks SCOT to use them. In DKA, high NADH from alcohol oxidation increases BHB, masking ketones on a standard urine dipstick.
cards.power: Brain Emergency Fuel — Convert excess Acetyl-CoA into soluble ketone bodies to bypass the blood-brain barrier.

cards.lore: Von Gierke disease (G6Pase deficiency) traps glucose in the liver, causing fasting hypoglycaemia, lactic acidosis, and a doll-like facies.
cards.power: Phosphorylase Cleave — Remove terminal glucose as G-1-P in response to glucagon or epinephrine.

cards.lore: Metformin inhibits ETC Complex I, impairing the mitochondrial malate-aspartate shuttle and starving PEPCK of oxaloacetate, thus lowering fasting glucose.
cards.power: Bypass Irreversibility — Use Pyruvate Carboxylase, PEPCK, FBPase-1, and G6Pase to force metabolism backward.

cards.lore: Fatty acid synthesis strictly requires NADPH, linking it dependently to the pentose phosphate pathway and malic enzyme.
cards.power: Malonyl-CoA Addition — Dephosphorylate ACC via insulin to activate the rate-limiting step of lipogenesis.

cards.lore: Statins competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase. This paradoxically lowers blood cholesterol primarily by triggering SREBP to upregulate hepatic LDL receptor clearance.
cards.power: SREBP Feedback — If cholesterol falls, cleave SREBP to enter the nucleus and upregulate LDL receptors.

cards.lore: Hyperammonaemia drives glutamine accumulation in astrocytes, causing massive osmotic cerebral oedema. Treat CPS-I deficiency with arginine.
cards.power: Nitrogen Excretion — Utilize CPS-I and NAG to commit toxic NH₃ to the urea cycle.

cards.lore: PKU (PAH deficiency) causes phenylalanine to cross the BBB, competitively inhibiting dopamine and serotonin synthesis, causing intellectual disability and hypopigmentation.
cards.power: Tyrosine Conversion — Use PAH and BH4 to convert essential phenylalanine to melanin, thyroid hormone, and dopamine.

cards.lore: In Acute Intermittent Porphyria, CYP inducers (barbiturates, phenytoin) accelerate ALAS1, causing neurotoxic PBG buildup. Never give phenytoin for AIP seizures.
cards.power: Heme Synthesis — Assemble protoporphyrin IX and load it with iron via ferrochelatase.

cards.lore: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome (absent HGPRT) forces purine degradation to uric acid, causing gout, and simultaneously destroys basal ganglia dopaminergic neurons causing self-mutilation.
cards.power: De Novo Salvage — Recycle hypoxanthine/guanine via HGPRT to save massive energy costs.

cards.lore: B12 deficiency causes a functional folate deficiency (megaloblastic anaemia) PLUS methylmalonate accumulation that demyelinates the dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts.
cards.power: Methyl Trap — Trap THF as N5-methyl-THF if Vitamin B12 is absent.

cards.lore: Midgut carcinoid tumors rarely cause systemic carcinoid syndrome until they metastasize to the liver, bypassing hepatic MAO clearance.
cards.power: Serotonin/NAD⁺ Shift — Divert 95% of substrate via the kynurenine pathway to generate immune tolerance and NAD⁺.

cards.lore: G6PD deficiency depletes NADPH. Oxidative stress (primaquine, fava beans) oxidizes hemoglobin into Heinz bodies, which splenic macrophages bite out, causing haemolytic anaemia.
cards.power: NADPH Regeneration — Run the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway to keep glutathione in a reduced, protective state.

cards.lore: Tay-Sachs (HEXA deficiency) causes GM2 ganglioside accumulation in CNS neurons, presenting as a cherry-red spot at the macula and fatal neurodegeneration.
cards.power: Substrate Accumulation — Fail to hydrolyze lipids, causing intralysosomal inclusions that progressively kill the cell.

cards.lore: Fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin) are bactericidal because they inhibit bacterial topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase), preventing the relaxation of supercoiling ahead of the replication fork.
cards.power: Semi-Conservative Replication — Use DNA Pol δ and ε to ensure high-fidelity genome duplication.

cards.lore: Lynch syndrome is caused by germline mismatch repair (MMR) gene mutations, causing microsatellite instability (MSI) and massive colorectal/endometrial cancer risk.
cards.power: Synthetic Lethality — Trap PARP onto DNA to force a double-strand break that BRCA-mutant cells cannot repair.

cards.lore: Alpha-amanitin from the death cap mushroom specifically blocks the elongating Ser2-P form of RNAPII, causing irreversible, delayed hepatocyte death.
cards.power: Promoter Binding — Recruit RNAPII to CpG islands to transcribe DNA into pre-mRNA.

cards.lore: Aminoglycosides bind the 30S subunit causing misreading and bactericidal death, whereas macrolides bind the 50S exit tunnel causing bacteriostatic arrest. Diphtheria toxin halts eukaryotic eEF2.
cards.power: Peptide Bond Formation — Use the peptidyltransferase ribozyme center to link amino acids.

cards.lore: CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib) force a G1 arrest in ER+ breast cancer by preventing pRb phosphorylation, restoring the gatekeeper function.
cards.power: Rb Phosphorylation — Hyperphosphorylate pRb via CDK4/6-cyclin D to release E2F and irreversibly commit to S phase.

cards.lore: MDM2 is an E3 ligase that constantly degrades p53. Hotspot mutations in the p53 DNA-binding domain exert dominant-negative oncogenic effects.
cards.power: Apoptotic Arrest — If DNA damage is unrepairable, transcribe BAX/PUMA for intrinsic apoptosis.

cards.lore: Taxanes (paclitaxel) stabilize microtubules preventing depolymerization, while vinca alkaloids prevent polymerization. Both abnormally alter tension, permanently arresting the cell in M-phase.
cards.power: Chromosome Segregation — Satisfy the Spindle Assembly Checkpoint to cleave cohesin and trigger anaphase.

cards.lore: PINK1 and Parkin mediate mitophagy of depolarized mitochondria. Mutations in these fail to clear toxic mitochondria, causing autosomal recessive Parkinson's disease.
cards.power: Phagophore Nucleation — Inhibit mTORC1 to activate ULK1 and lipidation of LC3-II to autophagosome membranes.

cards.lore: PROTAC drugs are bifunctional molecules that artificially drag undruggable target proteins to an E3 ligase, hijacking Uri to destroy them.
cards.power: Proteasomal Targeting — Attach K48-linked polyubiquitin chains to mark substrates for the 26S proteasome barrel.

cards.lore: IDH1/2 neomorphic mutations produce 2-hydroxyglutarate (an oncometabolite) that competitively inhibits TET2, causing DNA hypermethylation and a leukaemic differentiation block.
cards.power: Chromatin Remodeling — Acetylate histones to open chromatin; methylate CpG islands to permanently silence tumor suppressors.

cards.lore: The ceRNA hypothesis states that long non-coding RNAs act as sponges, soaking up miRNAs to derepress target oncogenes. miR-21 is a ubiquitous oncomiR.
cards.power: Translational Repression — Load the RISC complex to imperfectly bind target mRNAs, halting translation or triggering decay.

cards.lore: TERT promoter mutations (creating de novo ETS binding sites) are the most common non-coding mutations in cancer (melanoma, GBM), granting replicative immortality.
cards.power: TERT Reactivation — Express reverse transcriptase to extend the 3' overhang, evading permanent replicative senescence.

cards.lore: Multiple Myeloma cells survive at the brink of ER stress due to massive IgG secretion. Bortezomib pushes them over the edge into terminal UPR apoptosis.
cards.power: Unfolded Protein Response — Halt global translation via PERK/eIF2α while expanding ER chaperone capacity to restore proteostasis.

cards.lore: In I-cell disease (GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase deficiency), the M6P tag is never added. Hydrolases are secreted into blood instead, causing multi-system lysosomal storage failure.
cards.power: M6P Tagging — Add mannose-6-phosphate in the cis-Golgi to route acid hydrolases exclusively to lysosomes.

cards.lore: MELAS (m.3243A>G) impairs mitochondrial tRNAs, starving the brain of ATP and causing stroke-like episodes in non-vascular distributions, strictly via maternal inheritance.
cards.power: Heteroplasmic Shift — Segregate mutant mtDNA randomly during division; clinical severity depends entirely on the mutant-to-wild-type ratio threshold.

cards.lore: Mutations in tissue-specific intermediate filaments cause distinct diseases: Keratin (epidermolysis bullosa), Desmin (cardiomyopathy), and Lamin A (Progeria/rapid aging).
cards.power: Dynamic Instability — Rapidly alternate between GTP-driven polymerization and GDP-driven catastrophe to search intracellular space.

cards.lore: X-linked Adrenoleukodystrophy (ABCD1 mutation) traps VLCFAs outside the peroxisome, causing toxic accumulation that destroys the adrenal cortex and cerebral myelin.
cards.power: Alpha/Beta Oxidation — Import and break down very-long-chain and branched fatty acids that mitochondria cannot process.

cards.lore: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (dynein arm mutation) halts embryonic leftward nodal flow, meaning situs inversus occurs randomly in exactly 50% of patients.
cards.power: Mechanosensory Sweep — Move extracellular fluid or sense tubular flow via Polycystin 1/2 complexes to prevent aberrant proliferation.

cards.lore: Classic galactosaemia (GALT deficiency) causes neonatal liver failure, cataracts, and a highly specific vulnerability to fatal E. coli sepsis due to impaired neutrophil killing.
cards.power: Substrate Toxicity — Trap phosphorylated sugars intracellularly, depleting ATP and causing severe hepatotoxicity.

cards.lore: Serum ceruloplasmin is LOW in Wilson's disease because without ATP7B to load copper, unstable apoceruloplasmin is secreted and rapidly degraded in blood.
cards.power: Biliary Failure — Mutate ATP7B so copper cannot load into ceruloplasmin or excrete into bile, forcing toxic systemic spillover.

cards.lore: Propionic and Methylmalonic acidaemias cause profound hyperammonaemia because toxic propionyl-CoA directly inhibits CPS-I in the urea cycle.
cards.power: Keto-Acid Accumulation — Block BCKDH to force neurotoxic branched-chain keto acids into the blood and brain.

cards.lore: PMM2-CDG (Type Ia) presents with ataxia, coagulopathy, and inverted nipples. Underglycosylation of transferrin (type I peak on IEF) is the definitive screening diagnostic.
cards.power: Glycan Misfire — Fail to assemble N-linked oligosaccharides in the ER, devastating protein folding, secretion, and receptor function system-wide.

cards.lore: Cancer cells are not just anaerobic; MYC and HIF-1α rewire metabolism to actively use aerobic glycolysis and glutamine for massive biomass generation.
cards.power: Anaplerotic Theft — Siphon TCA intermediates for rapid biosynthesis, strictly requiring glutaminolysis to replenish the cycle.

cards.lore: Ferroptosis is a distinct, non-apoptotic cell death driven by lipid peroxides. It is triggered when GSH is depleted and GPx4 fails, requiring Fenton-reaction iron.
cards.power: Lipid Peroxidation — Deplete glutathione (GSH) to disable GPx4, unleashing iron-dependent ROS to destroy the plasma membrane.

cards.lore: Parkinson's disease spreads via the prion-like misfolding of α-synuclein into Lewy bodies. CHIP normally links chaperones to the proteasome to prevent this.
cards.power: Prion-like Spread — Escape chaperone surveillance to form toxic aggregates (Lewy bodies, plaques) that spread across post-mitotic networks.

cards.lore: No shortcut to pattern recognition is permitted — explain the mechanism. Case 1: Fasting hypoglycaemia = MCAD. Case 2: OCP + Rifampicin = AIP. Case 3: Myeloma + Bortezomib = Terminal UPR ER Stress.
cards.power: Integrated Clinical Reasoning — Connect the molecular defect directly to the patient's presentation.

cards.lore: Visceral adiposity triggers FFA release and ceramide accumulation, causing IRS-1 serine phosphorylation that fundamentally breaks the PI3K/Akt insulin signaling pathway.
cards.power: Ectopic Lipid Deposition — Overload visceral fat capacity to force toxic free fatty acids into liver and muscle, disabling insulin receptors.

cards.lore: The facts are real. The biology is flawless. The delivery is anarchy. Now go sabotage the boards. HUMBUG!
cards.power: Narrative Memory — You remember stories, not lists.
